checks.behavior: Use a student of level 5. Both lists show the same published stories of level 4 to 6 (AC-1). The new list shows books on shelves; a genre sign and a title search narrow it; an empty result shows a short note.
New: the Read page shows the sign "Articles | Stories" and the toolbar has four tabs.
Same title, summary, and chapter count (8) in both apps (AC-2).
Characters sign shows the characters in both apps.
Same text, picture, and audio. The highlight follows the audio in the new app (AC-3).
Pick th: the current sentence shows its translation in both apps.
Open the word list: the same words show with their meanings and audio.
Answer the 5 MCQ with the first option and submit. Both apps add score x 2 XP (4 of 5 correct gives 8 XP, AC-4). The steps record XP before and after on the page.
Retake the MCQ. Legacy adds XP again. New adds no XP and shows the new score (D4).
New: no answer reaches the client before the submit.

Fill a valid SAQ and LAQ answer. The steps record XP before and after but do not submit (the kit has no AI key). Feedback, submit XP, and the second-submit refusal are proven by the domain tests; the batch runner confirms them with a headed pass (AC-5).
The LAQ box shows the level x 30 minimum and the 2000-character cap (proven by the component tests).
The last chapter (8 of 8) shows "Previous chapter" and no "Next chapter" in both apps.
The chapter picture loads in the new app (a request for images/story/<legacy cuid>.png).

After the MCQ, SAQ, and LAQ of this chapter are all done, 3 to 5 new words and the chapter sentences save to the vocabulary and sentence decks with the chapter id as source_id. Check the decks and the flashcard tables (manual headed pass at batch time; Phase S6 builds the new save).
A word already in the deck saves no second card. With only one question type done, nothing saves.
The old chapter URL in the new app redirects to /student/read/stories/<uuid>/1 with the same chapter title as the legacy page.
Chapter 1 of 8 shows "Next chapter" and no "Previous chapter" in both apps.
An unknown story id shows the not-found page in both apps, with no redirect loop.
